objections.claim: A record only exists after students have already used the product, so the first term offers nothing to judge anyone on.
objections.evidence: Reliability is evidenced by completed projects and teammate confirmations

objections.claim: Students may read a visible record as a permanent punishment for one bad semester.
objections.evidence: students carry a visible record of the projects they actually finished

critiques.verdict: The sharpest wedge of the three, but it has a real cold-start problem.

objections.claim: The casting metaphor says nothing about reliability, which is the problem the founder actually described.
objections.evidence: Post the project you want to make and let the right crew answer the call.

objections.claim: Film language may signal creative projects and quietly exclude the engineering students this needs.
objections.evidence: Film-set language: calls, crews, credits and premieres

critiques.verdict: The most distinctive world, but it solves finding people rather than trusting them.

objections.claim: Any group-work tool could claim to make expectations explicit; nothing here is hard to copy.
objections.evidence: Teams agree what each person owes the group before the work starts

objections.claim: Students rarely adopt a tool that feels like homework administration before the trouble starts.
objections.evidence: Commitment layer for student group work

critiques.verdict: Closest to the stated pain, and the easiest of the three for a competitor to copy.

recommendation.reason: It is the only direction whose differentiator gets stronger with use, and its cold-start problem is fixable with a first-term onboarding.
